options: They let you reference a value once, so changing it updates everywhere it's used, instead of editing several hardcoded steps by hand
They automatically detect data types
They remove duplicate rows
They're required for every query, with no other purpose
questions.explain: A hardcoded value is baked into a specific step. A parameter is a named, reusable value — change it once in Manage Parameters, and every step referencing it updates automatically.

questions.q: Where do you create and manage parameters?
options: The Manage Parameters dialog, on the Home ribbon
The Advanced Editor only
The Data type dropdown
Parameters can't be edited after creation
questions.explain: Manage Parameters (Home ribbon) is where you create new parameters and view or edit existing ones.

questions.q: In the Filter Rows dialog, how do you use a parameter instead of a typed value?
options: Select "Select a parameter" instead of "Enter a value," then choose the parameter from the dropdown
You must type the parameter's name manually into the value field
Parameters can't be used in filters, only in custom functions
You have to edit the M code directly to reference a parameter
questions.explain: Most filter dialogs offer a toggle between "Enter a value" and "Select a parameter" right next to the value field — no manual M editing required.

questions.q: You change a parameter's Current Value from 0.2 to 0.3. What happens to a query that filters using that parameter?
options: It updates and re-filters automatically, with no need to edit the filter step itself
Nothing — you must manually re-select the parameter in the filter step
The query breaks and must be rebuilt
Only new queries created afterward will use the updated value
questions.explain: This is the whole point of parameters: any step referencing the parameter automatically uses its current value, so editing the parameter once ripples through everywhere it's used.

questions.q: Besides filter values, what's another common use for parameters?
options: File paths/connection details, and as arguments for custom functions
Parameters can only ever be used in filters
Changing a column's data type
Renaming queries
questions.explain: Parameters are also commonly used to store reusable file paths or connection details, and as the inputs when you turn a query into a custom function.
